question: A tube of homeopathic pills from a chemist's shelf. What does its active ingredient line actually describe?
answer: Sugar, in practice. 30C means diluted a hundredfold, thirty times over: one part in a 1 followed by 60 zeros, far past the point where a single molecule is likely to remain. In 2015 Australia's national medical research council reviewed homeopathy for 61 conditions and found no reliable evidence it worked for any.
move: Weigh studies by how well they were run, not by how many.
ask: When I count the evidence for something I like, do I weigh the careful studies more than the rest?

scene.head: Homeopathic medicine
scene.title: Arnica 30C
scene.body: Active ingredient: Arnica montana 30C. Homeopathic remedy for bruises and muscle aches. Gentle, with no known side effects.

phrases.why: Labels must list it. Diluted this far, it is a name, not a dose.
One part in a number with 60 zeros. Past about 12C, not one molecule is likely to be left.

phrases.plain: Sugar pill, shown to work no better than placebo
phrases.why: Australia's NHMRC reviewed 61 conditions in 2015 and found no reliable evidence for any.
Nothing in it can act on the body, for good or ill. Gentle is the honest word.

scene.ask: One three-character code says the pill holds nothing. Which?
scene.watch: When a label lists an ingredient, ask how much of it is actually in there.

reference: National Health and Medical Research Council, NHMRC Information Paper: Evidence on the effectiveness of homeopathy for treating health conditions, Canberra, 2015
